nodes.description: Respiratory fluoroquinolones such as levofloxacin, a first-line alternative for Legionnaires' disease, are cell-penetrant and kill intracellular Legionella by trapping the DNA gyrase/topoisomerase IV cleavage complex — the bactericidal fluoroquinolone target this node represents.

evidence.reference_title: Topoisomerase Inhibitors: Fluoroquinolone Mechanisms of Action and Resistance.
evidence.snippet: Quinolones dually target DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV binding to specific domains and conformations so as to block DNA strand passage catalysis and stabilize DNA-enzyme complexes that block the DNA replication apparatus and generate double breaks in DNA that underlie their bactericidal activity.

nodes.description: Tetracycline antibiotic that penetrates host cells and inhibits bacterial protein synthesis; a cell-penetrant alternative agent for Legionnaires' disease when macrolides or fluoroquinolones are unsuitable.

nodes.description: Legionnaires' disease results from inhalation of Legionella-contaminated aerosols followed by bacterial replication inside alveolar macrophages, where the organism establishes a replication-permissive intracellular compartment (the Legionella-containing vacuole). This obligate intracellular lifestyle is the basis for the requirement for cell-penetrant antibiotics, because beta-lactams cannot reach the cytoplasmic organism.

evidence.snippet: The Dot/Icm T4BSS translocates an exceptionally large number of effectors, more than 300 per L. pneumophila strain, and is essential for evasion of phagolysosomal degradation and exploitation of protozoa and human macrophages as replicative niches.

nodes.description: Because Legionella replicates inside host cells, effective treatment requires antibiotics that accumulate intracellularly — macrolides (e.g., azithromycin) and fluoroquinolones (e.g., levofloxacin) — whereas beta-lactams, which penetrate cells poorly, are ineffective. This pharmacokinetic gating, rather than a single enzyme target, governs drug selection.

evidence.reference_title: Atypical pneumonia: Pathophysiology, diagnosis, and treatment.

evidence.snippet: β-lactam and aminoglycoside antibiotics are not effective in the treatment of Legionella pneumonia due to their inability to permeate the cell membrane.

nodes.description: Legionella replication in the lung produces a severe lobar pneumonia that frequently requires intensive care. A characteristic feature is prominent extrapulmonary involvement — gastrointestinal and neurologic abnormalities and relative bradycardia — that helps distinguish Legionnaires' disease from other community-acquired pneumonias.
nodes.id: Severe Lobar Pneumonia with Extrapulmonary Features
